newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks end marginally up after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks end marginally up after choppy session.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended a choppy session slightly higher after bargain hunting was matched by further selling by foreign funds, dealers and analysts said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 leading stocks closed up 1.11 points at 1,087.78, after fluctuating between 1,069.58 and 1,102.11.
"I don't see any rebound being sustained," said an institutional dealer with a bank-backed brokerage house.
"We still have a lot of unfinished sell orders, and the buying from local institutions and retail investors was nowhere near matching it," he said.
Analysts said cash calls on leveraged investors continued to pressure the market while rumours about cash flow problems at several brokers were still circulating.
"The rumour has magnified fears among fund managers about the local market," said an analyst at a local firm.

He said the next support level is 1,050, which if broken, may lead to a further drop to 980-1,000. But he added that the market, currently trading at around its historical low price-earnings ratio of 15 times, could be bottoming out.
The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange said on Tuesday that no stockbroking firm had been suspended from trading.
At the close, market volume stood at 348 million shares, valued at 2.07 billion ringgit. Gainers led losers 354 to 288.
Newly-listed rubber glove maker Rubberex Corp ended its first day of trading at 6.10 ringgit against a 2.25 ringgit offer price. It traded as high as 7.20 ringgit.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot April contract rose 3.9 points to close at 1,092.4 on volume of 1,132 lots, while the May futures contract was up 8.5 points to 1,094.9 with 23 lots traded.
